Gordtopia · the register at 154 · drawn 6 September 2026

Villages and Gates of Gordtopia

19 villages, 5 outposts and camps, 13 gates, every one at a position the record actually holds, and what to do with each. All roads lead home; this is the list of where they stop on the way.

Part oneThe villages, west to east

Nineteen villages and four camps. Six of them carry names you gave; the rest carry the description they were read with. Every entry gives the nether-side address at the 1 to 8 ratio, because that is the number a hub needs.

How to engage a village, in the order that pays

  1. Ring the bell and log it. The bell is the village's address and its alarm; on Bedrock a rung bell makes nearby raiders glow. Your own bell is where every distance in this document starts.
  2. Sleep there once. A bed sets your spawn. A far village with a bed you have slept in is insurance for the whole walk back.
  3. Decide trade there or trade at home. A villager 12,000 blocks out is a boat and a nether ride from the hall. The Record's rule holds: the trading hall is a district, the breeder village is somewhere else, and cure discounts stack per villager, not per village, so the villager you cure is the villager you keep.
  4. Roll the one profession that ship maps. Cartography table beside an unemployed villager, break and replace to reroll, before the first trade locks them in. Fastest path to Master is paper at Novice, glass panes through Expert, banners to close the gap. Bring a compass per map.
  5. Run the raid on purpose, once, at Sunflower Hold. The Record already calls it the raid-risk village. Bell, golems, and the Hero of the Village discount that follows.
  6. Leave the far ones alone. Faredge Hold, the savanna village on the bay, the far village and the sleeping village are further than any villager should be walked. They are waypoints and bed stops. Their value is the hub you put within a hundred blocks of them.

Part twoThe gates, west to east

13 gates: 4 lit, 4 unlit by choice, and 5 that are something else, a broken island frame, an obsidian mass, a reading taken from inside the violet, a monumental portal in sight of the bell, and a station. Three of them wear a gold block at the crown, and that line runs 17,084 blocks from Sleepgate to the lit gate at 14,107.

How to engage a gate

  • Eight blocks there is one block here. Every entry below gives its nether side as X over 8, Z over 8. Build the nether side yourself at that address before you light the overworld frame; otherwise the game links to whatever portal it finds within range on the nether side, which is exactly how the gate at 14,107 came out of a portal that belonged to 13,547.
  • An enclosed landing room at every hub. The Record's own rule, and the portal station at 11,827 is the only place that already obeys it: frame, pillar, chest, gold block.
  • The unlit gates stay unlit until you say so. The doctrine written for Sleepgate covers 93 and 116 too. Lighting one is a naming act; log the date.
  • Ruined portals are chests first. On Bedrock the chest always generates and crying obsidian replaces a fifth of the frame. The ravine portal at 13,053 and the Crimson Gate island at 353 are the two ruined frames in the register.
  • One nether portal can serve a district. The shared portal at nether 1692, 165 already serves two overworld doors 563 blocks apart. Give it a room and two signposted exits and it is the far east's hub.

Part threeThe trunk: what the ratio buys

The whole walk home from the snow vantage at 17,848 to the last dune at 651 was 17,197 blocks of X across two nights. In the nether the same distance is about 2,150 blocks, a straight tunnel from the shared portal at 1692, 165 to Grandgate's nether side at 82, 278. The table is measured from the bell at the Works Board's sprint of 5.62 blocks a second, no boats, no ice.

Where the hubs already are

  • Vermilion hub near nether -959, 57, serving Vermilion Springs and the Cinnabar Deep in the far west.
  • The shared portal at nether 1692, 165, serving both gold-crowned gates and, by distance, the coastal savanna village (nether 1539, 153) and the ravine portal (nether 1631, 203).
  • Grandgate, nether 82, 278, in sight of the bell, and the natural head of an eastern trunk.
  • The station at 11,827, nether 1478, 179, already built to the rule.

The lattice, applied to the far villages

Part fourPlates

Twelve engraved plates, drawn after the record and not from the screen. Where the record has a photograph, the plate follows it; where it has a plan, the plate draws the plan. Nothing here is a screenshot.

Appendix: what the record does not carry

No village in the register has a logged population, a bed count, or a list of professions; those are read on the ground, not from a frame. Two villages, 121 and 115, have never been walked. The far-bank buildings at 147 on the walk home are read by eye from a small frame and may not be a village. The lights at 144 are not identified. Twelve clips from the second night, IMG_3106 to 3117, did not arrive, and four that did (3119, 3125, 3130, 3131) are too small to read a position from. The plates are illustrations; the coordinates are the record.

Sources: the register, landmarks.json at 154 entries; the two walk tracks read once a second, 407 positions; the Gordtopia Complete Record for the trading hall, the lattice, cure stacking, cartographers, raids and the nether rules; the Minecraft Wiki for the current wandering trader stock and ruined portal loot on Bedrock.
